artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\Sigma=\{0,1,2,3\}$. A *word* is a finite sequence over $\Sigma$, and a *circular word* of length $n$ is an equivalence class of words in $\Sigma^n$ under cyclic rotation. Given a pattern alphabet of variables $\{a,b,c,X,Y,Z,T\}$, a word $w\in\Sigma^*$ *encounters* the pattern $p=abXbcYcaZbaTac$ if there exist a non-erasing morphism $h$ from the variable alphabet to $\Sigma^+$ which is injective on $\{a,b,c\}$ (i.e., $h(a),h(b),h(c)$ are pairwise distinct) and possibly erasing on $\{X,Y,Z,T\}$, such that $h(p)$ occurs as a factor of $w$; otherwise $w$ *avoids* $p$. A circular word avoids $p$ if every linearization (every factor read along the cycle) avoids $p$.

Let $A(n)$ be the set of $n\in\mathbb{N}\setminus\{0\}$ for which there exists a circular word over $\Sigma$ of length $n$ that avoids the pattern $abXbcYcaZbaTac$. Prove that $A$ has density $0$ in $\mathbb{N}\setminus\{0\}$, i.e.,
$$\lim_{N\to\infty}\frac{|A\cap\{1,2,\dots,N\}|}{N}=0.$$
